hints.title: Row Seating Bit Encoding
hints.text: Classroom rows have at most eight desks. A bit sequence where set bits designate seated students neatly models any row configuration.

hints.title: Adjacent and Diagonal Sightline Invariants
hints.text: Students cannot sit next to each other in the same row, nor diagonally adjacent to students in the preceding row.

hints.title: Row by Row Submask DP Procedure
hints.text: For each row, filter broken seats into a valid seat mask. Enumerate every submask with no adjacent bits. Ensure no intersection with prev_mask shifted left or right by one. Advance row by row, adding the number of seated students to the optimal result of the next row. Return maximum students.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: input size or search state bound
complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(M * 2^(2N)) time and O(M * 2^N) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Trying all seat configurations naively has 2^(m*n) states, which equals 2^64 in the worst case.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Row-by-row bitmask DP stores O(m * 2^n) states and transitions in O(m * 2^(2n)) time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should model seating constraints using bitwise shifts and submask enumeration per row.
